cases.text: The primary-care clinician asks the consultant to assess the persistent problem outlined in the accompanying history. This letter explains why specialist input is being requested.
Dear colleague, please see this person in your outpatient service. Background history and the question for your specialist opinion are set out in this correspondence.
Consultation request: a community doctor is sending a patient to another specialty. The narrative describes the presenting concern and relevant past history.
This covering letter states the referring practitioner's clinical question and the background that prompted a request for a specialist appointment.
Reconciled prescription record: the person continues to take Example Agent Alpha and Example Agent Beta at home. This is the active regular-treatment list, not prescribing advice.
Routine medicines on the current chart are Fictional Compound A and Fictional Compound B. The referring office checked what is being taken at the last visit.
The home-drug reconciliation sheet lists all ongoing prescribed preparations. These fictional entries illustrate what staff should find in a current medication record.
Active treatments register: recorded regular prescriptions were reviewed with the person and updated by the referring team. The chart contains fictional placeholder products.
Sensitivity register: Fictional Compound C was followed by an itchy skin reaction. The reaction history is documented here for the receiving team.
The adverse-response section records intolerance to an example substance. Staff entered both the offending agent and the nature of the reaction in this fictional chart.
Allergen history was checked at the visit. No known drug allergies are recorded in this synthetic example, and the statement is documented by the referring office.
Past reactions to medicines are listed on this sensitivity sheet. It identifies the fictional trigger and the response that the person previously experienced.
Radiology findings: this signed imaging report contains observations from the diagnostic service and is enclosed with the referral. All findings are fictional.
The diagnostic laboratory has issued the attached findings sheet. It records the completed test results and the reporting date, without offering treatment recommendations.
An investigation results document is enclosed. It contains the diagnostic service's completed observations rather than a request for future testing.
Completed examination findings from the imaging department are transcribed on this report. The referring office has received the results for the packet.
Office cover sheet: record reference DEMO-200, telephone +1 202-555-0182, referring organization Mossvale Demo Clinic. These are fictional administrative contact details.
The registration face sheet records a callback number, a local patient reference, and the sending practice. It is the administrative contact page for this example packet.
Demographic routing slip: fictional case reference DEMO-200 and a callback telephone number are supplied alongside the originating clinic's name.
Intake administration page: the sending practice and patient callback details are written here so the receiving office can route correspondence to the correct record.
Release of information: the person has signed permission for the referring practice to disclose these records to the receiving specialist service for this referral.
A signed authorization permits transfer of the enclosed health documents between the sending clinic and the named receiving practice. This is a fictional permission form.
Records-sharing agreement: the person consents to the disclosure of the enclosed medical paperwork to the specialist office, with a signature and date recorded.
The disclosure permission sheet is signed. It authorizes the clinic to provide copies of the relevant health record to the receiving team for this outpatient referral.
